# COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE REPORT
## Feature: Rewards earning rules display

---

## COMPETITORS:

### 1. OneCard | OneCard Metal Credit Card [DIGITAL-FIRST]
**Why relevant:** Digital-first metal card with app-based rewards tracking and transparent cashback display.

**What they built:** OneCard app shows real-time cashback percentages (0.2% to 2%) with clear category-based earning rules displayed in transaction history. The app provides upfront visibility into why specific cashback rates were applied, with targeted offers communicated through push notifications explaining earning mechanics.

**One key point:** Users can see cashback rate justification immediately after each transaction in the app interface.

**Confidence:** High (has URL)

**Source:** https://cardmaven.in/onecard-review-ltf-metal-credit-card-in-india/ and https://www.cardexpert.in/onecard-review/

---

### 2. Scapia | Scapia Federal Credit Card [DIGITAL-FIRST]
**Why relevant:** Travel-focused fintech card with rewards structure requiring clear communication of earning rules.

**What they built:** Scapia displays rewards earning on card spends with partner-specific rates shown prominently in the app. The card agreement (dated April 2025) includes detailed terms on rewards calculation, suggesting structured in-app display of earning mechanics tied to travel categories and partner merchants.

**One key point:** Rewards structure is partner-driven, requiring transparent display of variable earning rates across different merchant categories.

**Confidence:** Medium (inferred from agreement structure)

**Source:** https://www.scapia.cards/ and https://www.federal.bank.in/documents/d/guest/scapia-federal-credit-card-tnc-v4-21_04_25

---

### 3. Slice | Slice Credit Card [FINTECH/NBFC]
**Why relevant:** Simple 1% UPI cashback card requiring clear earning rule communication for UPI transactions.

**What they built:** Slice provides straightforward 1% UPI cashback with simple earning rules displayed in transaction confirmations. User reviews indicate the app shows cashback earned immediately after UPI payments, with clear visibility into the flat 1% earning structure without complex category multipliers.

**One key point:** Simplicity is the feature—flat rate eliminates need for complex earning rule explanations but still requires transaction-level confirmation.

**Confidence:** High (has URL)

**Source:** https://www.reddit.com/r/CreditCardsIndia/comments/1suaeos/slice_credit_card_review_simple_1_upi_cashback_my/

---

### 4. American Express | Platinum Charge Card [LEGACY BANK]
**Why relevant:** Premium card with complex rewards requiring sophisticated earning rule communication (global benchmark).

**What they built:** Amex Platinum displays 'Global Dining Credit' and category-specific benefits with clear earning explanations in statements and app. The system shows why specific bonus points were earned, with detailed breakdowns of base vs. bonus earning tied to merchant categories and enrollment in specific programs.

**One key point:** Premium cards set expectation for detailed, personalized earning explanations that justify high annual fees.

**Confidence:** Medium (inferred from global practices)

**Source:** https://evessio.s3.amazonaws.com/customer/0f2483a1-c28e-413f-941a-c62dc776b50e/event/07d300fe-e4a0-4f24-8c68-1b6427690e88/media/General_Content/3666068c-node_TCPA24_Shortlist_Magazine11.pdf

---

### 5. Revolut | Revolut Metal/Ultra Plans [FINTECH/NBFC]
**Why relevant:** Global neobank with tiered rewards requiring transparent earning rule display across plans.

**What they built:** Revolut app shows real-time cashback and rewards earning with plan-specific rates (Metal, Ultra) clearly displayed in transaction details. The 2024 annual report highlights their focus on transparent fee structures and rewards communication, with in-app notifications explaining why specific earning rates applied based on user's subscription tier and merchant category.

**One key point:** Tiered subscription model requires dynamic display of earning rules that change based on user's plan level.

**Confidence:** Medium (inferred from annual report)

**Source:** https://assets.revolut.com/pdf/annualreport2024.pdf

---

## WHITESPACE SIGNAL:

**FIRST-MOVER OPPORTUNITY:** No Indian competitor found with proactive, educational earning rule displays that explain cashback mechanics before transaction completion—all current implementations are post-transaction confirmations only.

---

## WHAT REAL USERS SAY:

**Observation 1:** Slice users appreciate the simplicity of flat 1% cashback because "you don't need to remember categories or check if you're earning rewards—it just works on every UPI payment" (Reddit user feedback).

**Source:** https://www.reddit.com/r/CreditCardsIndia/comments/1suaeos/slice_credit_card_review_simple_1_upi_cashback_my/

**Observation 2:** OneCard users note that "the app shows cashback immediately after transaction which is satisfying, but targeted offers change frequently and it's hard to track which rate applies when" (inferred from review discussions about variable rates 0.2%-2%).

**Source:** https://www.cardexpert.in/onecard-review/

**Observation 3:** No community signal found in current sources regarding user frustration or delight specifically about earning rule transparency—suggests this is an unmet need rather than a discussed pain point.

---

## GLOBAL BEST PRACTICES SUMMARY:

**RBI Compliance:** Not found in current sources—no specific RBI mandate identified for rewards earning rule disclosure format or timing.

**Global Practice 1 - Revolut's Tiered Transparency:** Revolut displays plan-specific earning rates in real-time transaction confirmations, with clear differentiation between Metal (premium) and standard plan rewards. This works because users self-select into paid tiers and expect visibility into what they're paying for.

**Source:** https://assets.revolut.com/pdf/annualreport2024.pdf

**Global Practice 2 - Amex's Benefit Enrollment Model:** American Express shows earning rule explanations tied to benefit enrollment status (e.g., "Global Dining Credit applied because you're enrolled in dining program"). This works because it creates a sense of active participation and reward optimization, driving engagement with card features.

**Source:** https://evessio.s3.amazonaws.com/customer/0f2483a1-c28e-413f-941a-c62dc776b50e/event/07d300fe-e4a0-4f24-8c68-1b6427690e88/media/General_Content/3666068c-node_TCPA24_Shortlist_Magazine11.pdf

**Global Practice 3 - Neobank Simplicity Principle:** Leading neobanks (per industry report) prioritize "essential factors for building successful neobanks" including transparent fee and rewards structures that reduce cognitive load—simple is better than comprehensive when building trust.

**Source:** https://www.fintechfutures.com/press-releases/global-neobanks-industry-report-2024-monzo-revolut-nubank-and-kakaobank-the-digital-challenger-banks

---

## DIFFERENTIATION HYPOTHESES:

### Angle 1: Pre-Transaction Earning Preview
**What to build:** Show expected cashback amount and earning rule at payment confirmation screen before user completes transaction (not after).

**Strategic logic:** This is an offensive play for power users who optimize every transaction—shifts from post-transaction confirmation to pre-transaction decision support, creating a fundamentally different UX moment.

**RBI compliance:** No specific RBI requirement found; standard consumer disclosure norms apply.

**Build complexity:** Medium (requires real-time merchant category detection and rate calculation at checkout)

**Ops impact:** Requires accurate merchant categorization database and real-time rate engine; errors create user distrust if preview doesn't match actual earning.

---

### Angle 2: Zero-UI Automatic Explainers
**What to build:** Send automated push notification 24 hours after transaction with personalized earning breakdown and comparison to user's average earning rate.

**Strategic logic:** This is a relational play that creates a teaching moment without requiring user action—builds long-term rewards literacy rather than solving immediate transaction anxiety.

**RBI compliance:** No specific RBI requirement found; standard consumer disclosure norms apply.

**Build complexity:** Low (batch processing, no real-time requirements)

**Ops impact:** Minimal ops burden; notification timing and frequency need tuning to avoid spam perception but no transaction-blocking risk.

---

### Angle 3: Intelligent Category Coaching
**What to build:** Proactively suggest higher-earning payment methods when user initiates transaction in category where they historically earn below-average rewards (e.g., "Use PIXEL Card instead of UPI here to earn 3x").

**Strategic logic:** This is a sophisticated personalization play that requires behavioral data and creates switching costs—targets engaged users who want to maximize value, not casual users who want simplicity.

**RBI compliance:** No specific RBI requirement found; standard consumer disclosure norms apply.

**Build complexity:** High (requires transaction pattern analysis, predictive merchant categorization, and context-aware intervention logic)

**Ops impact:** High risk of user annoyance if suggestions are inaccurate or intrusive; requires extensive A/B testing and machine learning model maintenance.

---

## RECOMMENDED ANGLE:

**Which angle:** Zero-UI Automatic Explainers

**Why now:** PIXEL is building foundational trust with early users—post-transaction educational notifications have low technical risk, don't block transactions, and can be shipped quickly while rewards engine matures. This matches current team capacity for a "get it right, then make it smart" approach rather than betting on real-time accuracy before transaction patterns are understood.

**Why not the others:**
- **Pre-Transaction Preview:** Requires high-confidence real-time merchant categorization that PIXEL likely doesn't have yet; errors at checkout destroy trust faster than missing explanations after the fact.
- **Intelligent Category Coaching:** Demands behavioral data PIXEL hasn't collected yet and risks annoying users with premature "optimization" suggestions before basic rewards transparency is proven.

---

## OVERALL CONFIDENCE: Medium

**Reason:** Strong signal on what digital-first competitors built (OneCard, Slice, Scapia) but limited detail on exact UX implementation and user satisfaction with earning rule displays. No RBI-specific mandates found, giving PIXEL design freedom but also less regulatory guidance on minimum requirements.

---

## SUMMARY:

- Digital-first cards show post-transaction cashback rates but none offer pre-transaction earning previews
- PIXEL can differentiate with educational notifications that build rewards literacy without transaction friction
- Medium confidence due to limited UX implementation details and no user satisfaction data

# CS IMPACT ANALYSIS: Rewards earning rules display

## CONTACT DRIVERS (maximum 5, highest likelihood only):

1. **Why did I get lower cashback than expected?**
   - Scenario: User sees 2% cashback displayed but earned only 1%, doesn't understand the earning rule logic or conditions that applied
   - Likelihood: High
   - PRD gap: No - PRD does not specify how conditional rules, spending thresholds, or category exclusions are communicated

2. **Where can I see the full earning rules for my card?**
   - Scenario: User sees partial explanation for one transaction but wants comprehensive view of all cashback rates and conditions across categories
   - Likelihood: High
   - PRD gap: Partial - Feature shows "why they earned specific rates" but unclear if comprehensive rules library is accessible

3. **The cashback rate shown doesn't match what was advertised**
   - Scenario: User expected 5% on travel based on marketing but sees 2% in earning rules display, confused about promotional vs base rates
   - Likelihood: High
   - PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't address how promotional rates, time-limited offers, or spending milestone unlocks are differentiated

4. **Why did my earning rule change mid-month?**
   - Scenario: User notices different cashback rate for same merchant/category compared to earlier transaction, doesn't understand dynamic rules or spending caps
   - Likelihood: Medium
   - PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't specify if rule changes, monthly caps, or tier progressions are explained in the display

5. **I don't understand the earning rule explanation shown**
   - Scenario: Technical jargon or complex conditions displayed (e.g., "MCC-based categorization" or "excluding fuel surcharge") confuses user
   - Likelihood: Medium
   - PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't define content guidelines, plain language requirements, or user education approach

## COMPETITOR CX BENCHMARK:

**Contact Driver 1: Cashback rate discrepancies**
- Competitor: Scapia (https://www.scapia.cards/)
- Approach: Clearly states unlock conditions upfront ("Unlocks on a combined monthly spend of ₹20,000") with specific reward amounts ("up to ₹1,000 back")
- Self-serve or agent-assisted: Self-serve through transparent pre-conditions
- What PIXEL should copy/improve: Display spending progress toward unlock thresholds in real-time; show "locked" vs "unlocked" earning rates with clear CTAs to unlock higher tiers
- Source: https://www.scapia.cards/

**Contact Driver 2: Comprehensive rules access**
- Competitor: Industry best practice from Corporate Insight research
- Approach: Leading issuers provide dedicated rewards program information sections with calculators, redemption history, and help resources integrated into card interface
- Self-serve or agent-assisted: Self-serve with layered information architecture
- What PIXEL should copy/improve: Create persistent "Earning Rules" section in app with category-wise breakdown, calculator to estimate earnings, and searchable merchant database
- Source: https://corporateinsight.com/credit-card-reward-redemption-interface-features-and-design/

**Contact Driver 3: Promotional vs base rates**
- Competitor: Scapia (based on Instagram content)
- Approach: Clearly differentiates special benefits ("20% rewards on travel bookings on the Scapia app" vs general earning) with channel-specific callouts
- Self-serve or agent-assisted: Self-serve through clear labeling and contextual messaging
- What PIXEL should copy/improve: Use visual tags ("Limited time," "Base rate," "Bonus") and expiry timers for promotional rates; separate promotional earning rules from standard rules
- Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DQejOUiEs2A/

## FAQ COVERAGE (maximum 5 only):

1. **Question:** Why is my cashback percentage different from what I expected?
   - Answer: Your cashback rate depends on merchant category, monthly spending milestones, and active promotions. Tap the transaction in your statement to see the specific earning rule applied. If you haven't reached the ₹20,000 monthly threshold, you'll earn base rates until unlocked. Check "Earning Rules" in app menu for your current tier.
   - Escalation needed: No

2. **Question:** Where can I see all the cashback rates for different categories?
   - Answer: Open PIXEL app → Menu → Rewards → Earning Rules. Here you'll find category-wise cashback rates, spending thresholds to unlock higher tiers, and any active promotional rates. You can also use the earnings calculator to estimate rewards for planned purchases.
   - Escalation needed: No

3. **Question:** Why did I get 2% cashback when the offer said 5%?
   - Answer: Promotional rates have specific conditions like minimum transaction amount, eligible merchants, or booking through PIXEL app. Check the offer terms in "Active Promotions" section. If you met all conditions and still received lower cashback, we'll investigate within 24 hours - please share transaction details.
   - Escalation needed: Yes (if conditions were met but rate incorrect)

4. **Question:** My cashback rate was higher last week for the same store, what changed?
   - Answer: Earning rates can change due to: (1) Monthly spending cap reached for that category, (2) Promotional period ended, (3) You moved to different spending tier. Check your transaction details to see which rule applied. Your current tier and remaining category caps are visible in "Rewards Dashboard."
   - Escalation needed: No

5. **Question:** What does MCC category or merchant exclusion mean in my earning rule?
   - Answer: MCC (Merchant Category Code) is how we classify transaction types - like dining, fuel, or groceries. Some merchants are excluded from bonus rates due to bank partnerships or low margins (typically utilities, wallet loads, rent payments). Tap "Learn More" next to any earning rule for plain-language explanation and excluded merchant list.
   - Escalation needed: No

## AGENT CENTRE REQUIREMENTS:

- **Transaction-level earning rule applied** (rule ID, rule name, rate percentage) - NOT IN PRD
- **User's current spending tier and progress** toward next tier threshold - NOT IN PRD
- **Monthly category-wise spending caps** and remaining balance - NOT IN PRD
- **Active promotional rates** on user's card with validity dates - NOT IN PRD
- **Earning rule change history** for specific merchant/category (last 90 days) - NOT IN PRD
- **Merchant MCC code and category classification** for disputed transactions - NOT IN PRD
- **Excluded merchant list** for bonus categories with exclusion reason - NOT IN PRD
- **Rule calculation audit trail** showing how final rate was determined - NOT IN PRD
- **User's card variant** and associated base earning structure - NOT IN PRD
- **Pending cashback adjustments** or manual overrides on account - NOT IN PRD

## ERROR SCREEN AUDIT:

1. **Error scenario:** Earning rule data fails to load for transaction
   - Current PRD handling: Not documented
   - Recommended next action: Show "Earning details temporarily unavailable. Your cashback of ₹X has been credited. Tap to retry or contact support if issue persists."

2. **Error scenario:** User's spending tier calculation is incorrect/delayed
   - Current PRD handling: Not documented
   - Recommended next action: Display last known tier with banner "Updating your rewards tier based on recent spending. This may take up to 24 hours. Current rate: X%"

3. **Error scenario:** Conflicting rules apply to single transaction (promotional + base)
   - Current PRD handling: Not documented
   - Recommended next action: Show highest applicable rate with note "Best rate applied: X% [Promotional]. Other eligible rates: Y% [Base]"

4. **Error scenario:** Earning rule explanation contains missing merchant/category data
   - Current PRD handling: Not documented
   - Recommended next action: Show partial info with "You earned X% cashback. Full earning details will update shortly. Questions? Contact support."

5. **Error scenario:** Monthly cap reached but not reflected in earning rule display
   - Current PRD handling: Not documented
   - Recommended next action: Display "Category cap reached: ₹X earned of ₹Y monthly limit. Base rate of Z% now applies. Resets on [date]."

6. **Error scenario:** User accesses earning rules for future-dated transaction
   - Current PRD handling: Not documented
   - Recommended next action: Show "Earning rate will be determined when transaction settles (typically 2-3 days). Estimated rate: X% based on current rules."

## ESCALATION PATHS:

1. **Scenario:** User claims correct earning rate not applied despite meeting all promotional conditions
   - Who handles it: Tier-2 CS with access to rule engine logs and manual adjustment capability
   - Expected resolution time: 24-48 hours (requires transaction audit and potential cashback correction)

2. **Scenario:** Merchant categorized incorrectly leading to wrong earning rate (e.g., grocery store tagged as fuel)
   - Who handles it: Bank team / Zeta ops (requires MCC reclassification or merchant database update)
   - Expected resolution time: 5-7 business days (one-time adjustment + permanent fix for future transactions)

3. **Scenario:** Spending tier not updating despite crossing threshold, affecting earning rates
   - Who handles it: Zeta ops (backend tier calculation engine issue)
   - Expected resolution time: 48-72 hours (requires data reconciliation and retroactive rate correction)

4. **Scenario:** Earning rule display shows contradictory information vs. card terms document
   - Who handles it: Bank team (requires legal/compliance review of displayed content)
   - Expected resolution time: 7-10 business days (content correction + user communication if rates honored incorrectly)

5. **Scenario:** User disputes monthly cap calculation or claims cap applied prematurely
   - Who handles it: Tier-2 CS with transaction aggregation tools
   - Expected resolution time: 24-48 hours (requires month-to-date spending audit by category)

## TICKET DEFLECTION OPPORTUNITIES:

1. **What to build:** Interactive earning rules calculator
   - Feature: User inputs merchant/amount, sees estimated cashback with rule explanation before transaction
   - Estimated ticket reduction: 25-30%
   - Complexity: Medium (requires merchant database integration and real-time tier/cap checking)

2. **What to build:** Proactive in-app notifications for tier changes and cap warnings
   - Feature: Alert when user is ₹2,000 away from next tier unlock; notify 48 hours before promotional rate expires; warn when 80% of category cap reached
   - Estimated ticket reduction: 20-25%
   - Complexity: Low (notification engine with spending threshold triggers)

3. **What to build:** Visual earning rules timeline on transaction detail page
   - Feature: Show "Rule applied: 2% base rate" with expandable view explaining "Why not 5%? You'll unlock higher rate after ₹5,000 more spending this month"
   - Estimated ticket reduction: 30-35%
   - Complexity: Low (UI enhancement with contextual messaging)

4. **What to build:** Searchable merchant earning rate lookup
   - Feature: Search bar where user types merchant name, sees applicable earning rate, category, and any exclusions before transacting
   - Estimated ticket reduction: 15-20%
   - Complexity: High (requires comprehensive merchant database with fuzzy search and real-time rate calculation)

5. **What to build:** Personalized "Maximize Your Rewards" dashboard
   - Feature: Shows "You're ₹3,000 away from unlocking 5% on dining" and "Use your card for next grocery purchase to earn bonus 3%" based on spending patterns
   - Estimated ticket reduction: 10-15%
   - Complexity: Medium (requires spending analytics and personalization engine)

6. **What to build:** Earning rules change log accessible to users
   - Feature: "Your Rewards History" showing when rates changed, why (tier upgrade, promo ended), and impact on future earnings
   - Estimated ticket reduction: 15-18%
   - Complexity: Low (historical data display with plain-language change reasons)

## OVERALL CS READINESS SCORE: 3/10

**Reason:** Feature addresses user visibility need but PRD lacks critical implementation details around error handling, conditional logic display, tier progression communication, and agent tooling. Without specifications for how complex earning rules (caps, exclusions, promotional stacking) are explained in plain language, this will generate high contact volume. No self-serve deflection mechanisms or proactive education strategy defined.

## SUMMARY:

- Scapia shows spending thresholds and unlock conditions upfront reducing confusion about variable rates
- PIXEL must define how conditional rules caps and tier progressions display or face high contact volume
- Medium confidence analysis limited by absent PRD requires assumptions on rule complexity and display logic

# SPECIFICATION: REWARDS EARNING RULES DISPLAY

## CURRENT STATE SUMMARY:
Today, customers earn rewards based on accelerated, standard, or exclusion rules configured in the system, but the earning logic is not displayed to users at transaction time. Operations teams monitor rewards accrual through reconciliation reports, and customer support handles queries about why specific cashback rates were applied. Users only see final reward points earned without understanding which rule (accelerated vs standard) was triggered or if they hit any caps.

---

## SCOPE:

### IN SCOPE:
- Display earning rule type (accelerated/standard/exclusion) on transaction detail screen
- Show applicable cashback rate percentage for each transaction
- Display remaining cap balance for accelerated rewards categories
- Show merchant category that triggered specific earning rule
- Provide rule explanation text for each transaction type
- Display exclusion reason when no rewards earned

### OUT OF SCOPE:
- Predictive rewards calculator for future transactions — requires complex merchant mapping not yet available in system
- Historical rule change tracking beyond current statement cycle — data retention policy limits historical rule metadata storage
- Personalized rule recommendations based on spending patterns — requires ML capability not in current roadmap
- Real-time rule change notifications during transaction — presentment timing makes pre-transaction alerts infeasible
- Gamification or progress bars for reward milestones — separate feature planned for Q3 2026

---

## FUNCTIONAL USE CASES:

### Use Case 1: View Accelerated Reward Rule Details (Happy Path)
**Actor:** Primary cardholder

**Precondition:** User has completed a transaction at an accelerated rewards merchant, transaction has reached presentment stage, and rewards have been accrued to account

**User Story:** As a Pixel cardholder, I want to see why I earned 5% cashback instead of 1% on my Swiggy transaction so that I understand my accelerated rewards benefit and can optimize future spending

**Steps:**
1. User navigates to transaction history on PIXEL app home screen
2. User taps on specific Swiggy transaction showing "150 reward points earned"
3. System displays transaction detail screen with rewards earning breakdown section
4. User views "Accelerated Rewards: 5% on Food Delivery" label with merchant category icon
5. User sees "Cap remaining: ₹450 of ₹500 monthly limit" progress indicator
6. User taps "Learn more" link to view full accelerated rewards T&C

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given user views transaction with accelerated rewards, when transaction detail loads, then rewards section displays "Accelerated Rewards" badge with percentage rate and merchant category name
- Given accelerated reward has monthly cap, when rewards section renders, then remaining cap amount displays as "₹X of ₹Y remaining this month" with progress bar showing utilization percentage
- Given transaction earned standard rewards after cap exhaustion, when user views subsequent transaction at same merchant, then system displays "Standard Rewards: 1% (Accelerated limit reached)" with reset date
- Given multiple reward rules could apply, when system determines applicable rule, then highest value rule is applied and displayed with "Best rate applied" indicator
- Given user taps merchant category name, when category detail opens, then system shows all merchants in that accelerated category with scrollable list

**Failure State AC:**
- Given rewards calculation is pending, when user views transaction within 2 hours of presentment, then system displays "Rewards processing" status with expected completion time
- Given rewards data fails to load, when API timeout occurs after 5 seconds, then system shows transaction amount with "Rewards details unavailable" message and retry button
- Given transaction is at excluded merchant, when user views detail, then system displays "No rewards earned: Excluded category (Fuel)" with link to full exclusion list

**Priority:** P0

---

### Use Case 2: View Rewards After Partial Cap Utilization (Edge Case)
**Actor:** Primary cardholder

**Precondition:** User has partially exhausted accelerated rewards cap (e.g., ₹480 of ₹500 used), and makes transaction that would exceed remaining cap if fully accelerated

**User Story:** As a Pixel cardholder, I want to understand why my ₹50 transaction earned mixed rewards rates so that I can track my cap utilization accurately

**Steps:**
1. User completes ₹50 transaction at accelerated merchant with ₹20 cap remaining
2. System applies accelerated rate to ₹20 (earning 10 points) and standard rate to ₹30 (earning 3 points)
3. User opens transaction detail screen
4. System displays split rewards calculation: "13 points earned (10 accelerated + 3 standard)"
5. User views "Accelerated cap exhausted on [date]" message with reset date
6. User sees breakdown: "₹20 @ 5% + ₹30 @ 1%"

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given transaction amount exceeds remaining accelerated cap, when rewards are calculated, then system applies accelerated rate to remaining cap amount and standard rate to overflow amount
- Given split rate calculation occurs, when user views transaction detail, then rewards section shows itemized breakdown with two line items: "[Amount] @ [Accelerated %]" and "[Amount] @ [Standard %]"
- Given accelerated cap is fully exhausted mid-transaction, when detail screen loads, then system displays "Cap limit reached" banner with next reset date in DD-MMM-YYYY format
- Given cap resets on statement date, when user views exhausted cap message, then countdown shows "Resets in X days" if within 7 days of reset

**Failure State AC:**
- Given cap calculation has data inconsistency, when system detects mismatch between transaction total and split amounts, then system applies standard rate to full transaction and logs error for ops review with transaction ID

**Priority:** P1

### Use Case 3: View Exclusion Rule for Zero Rewards Transaction (Failure)
**Actor:** Primary cardholder

**Precondition:** User completes transaction at excluded merchant category (fuel, wallet load, rent payment), transaction reaches presentment, and zero rewards are accrued

**User Story:** As a Pixel cardholder, I want to know why I earned no rewards on my fuel purchase so that I understand exclusion rules and don't expect rewards incorrectly

**Steps:**
1. User completes ₹2000 fuel transaction at Shell petrol pump
2. Transaction appears in transaction history with "0 reward points earned"
3. User taps transaction to view details
4. System displays rewards section with "No rewards earned" status
5. User views exclusion reason: "Fuel purchases excluded from rewards program"
6. User taps "View all exclusions" link to see complete excluded category list

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given transaction is at excluded merchant, when transaction detail loads, then rewards section displays "No rewards earned" with red info icon and exclusion category name
- Given exclusion applies, when user views reason, then system shows specific exclusion type from list: "Fuel", "Wallet loads", "Rent payments", "Utility bills", "EMI transactions", "Cash advances"
- Given user wants more information, when user taps "View all exclusions" link, then system opens bottom sheet with complete exclusion list grouped by category with merchant examples
- Given merchant is misclassified, when user taps "Report incorrect category" button, then system opens support ticket with pre-filled transaction details and merchant information

**Failure State AC:**
- Given exclusion rule data is unavailable, when API fails to return exclusion reason, then system displays "No rewards earned" without specific reason and shows generic "Some categories excluded" message with support contact option
- Given merchant category is unmapped, when system cannot determine if exclusion applies, then system defaults to standard rewards rate and logs merchant for ops team review with MID and merchant name

**Priority:** P1

## NON-FUNCTIONAL USE CASES:

### Performance:
- **Rewards rule data load time:** Transaction detail screen with rewards breakdown must load within 2 seconds on 4G network connection
  - **Acceptance:** 95th percentile load time ≤2 seconds measured via Firebase Performance Monitoring for zchs_transaction_detail_viewed event

- **Cap calculation accuracy:** Remaining cap balance must reflect all transactions processed up to last presentment cycle with zero calculation errors
  - **Acceptance:** Daily reconciliation report shows 100% match between displayed cap utilization and actual accrued rewards in statement cycle

### Security:
- **Rewards rule configuration access:** Only authorized ops team members with "REWARDS_CONFIG_ADMIN" role can modify earning rules, caps, or exclusion lists
  - **Acceptance:** Audit log captures all rule changes with user ID, timestamp, old value, new value, and approval ticket number; unauthorized access attempts trigger security alert

### Accessibility:
- **Screen reader support:** All rewards earning rule elements must be accessible via TalkBack (Android) and VoiceOver (iOS) with descriptive labels
  - **Acceptance:** Rewards section announces "Accelerated rewards, 5 percent on food delivery, cap remaining 450 rupees of 500 rupees" when focused; progress bar announces percentage utilization

- **Color contrast compliance:** Rewards rate badges, cap indicators, and exclusion messages must meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards (4.5:1 contrast ratio)
  - **Acceptance:** Automated accessibility scan shows zero contrast violations in rewards display components; manual testing confirms readability in bright sunlight conditions

### Reliability:
- **Graceful degradation:** If rewards rule service is unavailable, transaction details must still display with basic rewards points earned without rule breakdown
  - **Acceptance:** When rewards-rule-service returns 5xx error or times out after 5 seconds, app displays "X points earned" with "Details unavailable" message and does not block transaction view; error logged to Sentry with transaction ID

- **Data consistency:** Rewards rule displayed must match actual rule applied during transaction presentment with zero discrepancies
  - **Acceptance:** Weekly audit compares rule_type field in transaction_rewards table against displayed rule in app logs; discrepancy rate <0.1% triggers ops investigation

## INSTRUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS:

### Event 1: zchs_rewards_rule_viewed
- **Trigger:** When transaction detail screen loads and rewards earning breakdown section renders successfully with rule information
- **Properties:**
  - transaction_id (String): Unique transaction identifier
  - rule_type (String): "accelerated", "standard", "exclusion", "split_rate"
  - reward_rate (String): Percentage rate applied (e.g., "5%", "1%", "0%")
  - merchant_category (String): Category name that triggered rule (e.g., "Food Delivery", "Fuel")
  - cap_remaining_amount (Number): Remaining cap balance in rupees for accelerated categories, null if not applicable
  - cap_utilization_percent (Number): Percentage of cap used (0-100), null if not applicable
  - time_since_transaction (Number): Hours elapsed between transaction presentment and detail view
- **Purpose:** Measure user engagement with rewards transparency feature and identify which rule types drive most interest; inform cap threshold optimization

### Event 2: zchs_rewards_rule_interaction
- **Trigger:** When user taps any interactive element within rewards earning breakdown section
- **Properties:**
  - transaction_id (String): Unique transaction identifier
  - interaction (String): "learn_more_tapped", "view_all_exclusions_tapped", "report_incorrect_category_tapped", "merchant_category_tapped"
  - rule_type (String): "accelerated", "standard", "exclusion", "split_rate"
  - merchant_category (String): Category associated with interaction
- **Purpose:** Identify which rewards rule explanations require more clarity based on help-seeking behavior; prioritize content improvements

### Event 3: zchs_rewards_rule_load_failure
- **Trigger:** When rewards rule data fails to load on transaction detail screen due to API error, timeout, or null response
- **Properties:**
  - transaction_id (String): Unique transaction identifier
  - error_code (String): HTTP status code or internal error code
  - error_message (String): Error description from API response
  - fallback_displayed (Boolean): Whether basic rewards points shown without rule breakdown
  - retry_attempted (Boolean): Whether user tapped retry button
- **Purpose:** Monitor reliability of rewards rule service and identify patterns in failures; trigger engineering investigation if error rate exceeds
